name: React Interview Questions Quiz
description: A comprehensive React interview quiz with code snippets to test your understanding of React concepts, hooks, and components for frontend developer preparation.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false); const toggleModal = () => setIsOpen(!isOpen);```

acceptedAnswer.text: Toggles the visibility of a modal

suggestedAnswer.text: Changes the value of 'isOpen' to true
Sets 'isOpen' to false
None of the above

itemListElement.description: The function 'toggleModal' changes the value of 'isOpen' to its opposite (true/false), which could be used to control the visibility of a modal.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const [user, setUser] = useState({ name: '', age: 0 }); const handleChange = (event) => { const { name, value } = event.target; setUser((prevState) => ({ ...prevState, [name]: value })); }; return <input name="name" value={user.name} onChange={handleChange} />;```

acceptedAnswer.text: Updates the name in the 'user' state object

suggestedAnswer.text: None of the above
Resets the 'user' state object
Only changes the 'name' field in the state object

itemListElement.description: This code handles input changes and updates the 'name' property in the 'user' state object using the spread operator to maintain the other properties.

{children}

acceptedAnswer.text: Renders 'Hello World' inside a div

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = () => { const [text, setText] = useState(''); const handleChange = (e) => setText(e.target.value); return <input value={text} onChange={handleChange} />; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Creates a controlled input that updates state

suggestedAnswer.text: Renders an uncontrolled input field
None of the above
Automatically resets the text value to empty

itemListElement.description: The input's value is controlled by the 'text' state. The handleChange function updates the state as the user types.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const [counter, setCounter] = useState(0); useEffect(() => { document.title = `Counter: ${counter}`; }, [counter]);```

acceptedAnswer.text: Updates the document title to display the counter value

suggestedAnswer.text: Sets the counter to 0 when the component mounts
Tracks counter changes but doesn't update the document title
None of the above

itemListElement.description: The useEffect hook runs every time the 'counter' value changes, updating the document title with the current counter value.

itemListElement.text:
What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = () => { const [data, setData] = useState([]); useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/data') .then(response => response.json()) .then(result => setData(result)); }, []); return
{data.length > 0 ?

{data[0].name}

:

Loading...

}
; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Fetches data from an API and renders the first item's name

suggestedAnswer.text: Always shows 'Loading...' because the state is never updated
None of the above
Fetches and displays the data, but only shows 'Loading...' when there is an error

itemListElement.description: This code uses the useEffect hook to fetch data when the component mounts. It conditionally renders either the first item's name or 'Loading...' until the data is fetched.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(true); const toggleVisibility = () => setIsVisible((prev) => !prev); return <button onClick={toggleVisibility}>Toggle</button>;```

acceptedAnswer.text: Toggles the visibility of an element

suggestedAnswer.text: None of the above
Sets 'isVisible' to true when clicked
Only toggles the visibility once

itemListElement.description: This code uses a button to toggle the 'isVisible' state between true and false each time it is clicked.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const [userData, setUserData] = useState(null); useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/user') .then(response => response.json()) .then(data => setUserData(data)); }, []);```

acceptedAnswer.text: Both a and c

suggestedAnswer.text: Fetches data from an API and stores it in state
Displays an error if the API call fails
Sets the user data when the component mounts

itemListElement.description: The useEffect hook fetches data from an API when the component mounts and updates the 'userData' state with the fetched data.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const handleClick = () => { alert('Button clicked!'); }; return <button onClick={handleClick}>Click Me</button>;```

acceptedAnswer.text: Displays a button that shows an alert on click

suggestedAnswer.text: Changes the button text to 'Clicked'
Logs a message to the console on click
None of the above

itemListElement.description: The code defines a function 'handleClick' that triggers an alert when the button is clicked.

{title}

acceptedAnswer.text: Sets the default title if no prop is passed

Renders a static title

itemListElement.description: The defaultProps feature is used to specify default values for props in case they are not passed.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const [name, setName] = useState(''); const handleChange = (event) => setName(event.target.value); return <input value={name} onChange={handleChange} />;```

acceptedAnswer.text: All of the above

suggestedAnswer.text: Creates an input field that updates state on change
Displays a static value in the input field
Sets the value of the input to the 'name' state

itemListElement.description: The code binds the input field's value to the 'name' state and updates it whenever the user types in the input.

itemListElement.text:
What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = () => { const memoizedValue = useMemo(() => computeExpensiveValue(a, b), [a, b]); return
{memoizedValue}
; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Memoizes the result of computeExpensiveValue for performance optimization

suggestedAnswer.text: Updates the component on each render
Caches the value of 'a' and 'b'
None of the above

itemListElement.description: The useMemo hook is used to memoize expensive calculations, re-calculating the value only when 'a' or 'b' change, improving performance.

itemListElement.text:
What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = () => { const [isToggled, setIsToggled] = useState(false); const handleClick = () => setIsToggled((prev) => !prev); return
{isToggled ? "Toggled!" : "Not Toggled"}

acceptedAnswer.text: Displays 'Toggled!' when the state is true and 'Not Toggled' when false

suggestedAnswer.text: Always displays 'Toggled!'
Sets the state to true only once
None of the above

itemListElement.description: This component toggles between 'Toggled!' and 'Not Toggled' based on the value of 'isToggled' state.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = () => { const [counter, setCounter] = useState(0); useEffect(() => { console.log(counter); }, []); return <button onClick={() => setCounter(counter + 1)}>Increment</button>; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Logs the counter value only once, when the component mounts

suggestedAnswer.text: Logs the counter value every time it changes
Logs 'undefined' because the state is never updated
None of the above

itemListElement.description: The empty dependency array in useEffect ensures that the log is only executed once when the component mounts, regardless of state changes.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = () => { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); const increment = () => setCount(count + 1); return <button onClick={increment}>Increment</button>; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Increments the count value by 1 each time the button is clicked

suggestedAnswer.text: Sets the count value to 1 on every click
Prevents the button from being clicked
None of the above

itemListElement.description: The increment function increases the 'count' state by 1 every time the button is clicked.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = () => { const [name, setName] = useState(''); const handleChange = (e) => setName(e.target.value); return <input type="text" value={name} onChange={handleChange} />; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Updates the input field value with the 'name' state on each change

suggestedAnswer.text: Sets the input value to an empty string
Prevents any changes to the input field
None of the above

itemListElement.description: The input's value is controlled by the 'name' state, and the handleChange function updates it as the user types.

itemListElement.text:

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = () => { const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState(''); const handleSubmit = (event) => { event.preventDefault(); alert(inputValue); }; return ( <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}> <input value={inputValue} onChange={(e) => setInputValue(e.target.value)} /> <button type="submit">Submit</button> </form> ); };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Displays an alert with the input value when the form is submitted

suggestedAnswer.text: Prevents the form submission but doesn't handle the input value
Resets the input value every time it is submitted
None of the above

itemListElement.description: The handleSubmit function prevents the default form submission behavior and shows an alert with the input value.

itemListElement.text:
What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = React.memo(({ count, increment }) => { console.log('Rendering MyComponent'); return (

{count}

); });```

acceptedAnswer.text: The component will only re-render when props 'count' or 'increment' change

suggestedAnswer.text: None of the above
The component will re-render on every state update
The component never re-renders

itemListElement.description: React.memo is a higher-order component that memoizes the component to prevent unnecessary re-renders when the props do not change.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const Counter = () => { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); const increment = useCallback(() => setCount(c => c + 1), []); return <button onClick={increment}>{count}</button>; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: The increment function is memoized, preventing re-creation on every render

suggestedAnswer.text: None of the above
The increment function is re-created every time the component renders
The counter doesn't increment due to an error

itemListElement.description: The useCallback hook memoizes the increment function, ensuring it is not re-created on every render, improving performance when passed to child components.

itemListElement.text: What will be the result of the following code? ```const Counter = () => { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); useEffect(() => { console.log(count); }, [count]); return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</button>; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Logs the count value every time it changes

suggestedAnswer.text: Logs 'undefined' because count is not set initially
None of the above
Logs '0' only once when the component mounts

itemListElement.description: The useEffect hook listens for changes to the 'count' state and logs it whenever the state updates, thanks to the dependency array [count].

itemListElement.text: What will be the result of the following code? ```const Counter = () => { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); const increment = () => setCount(count + 1); const memoizedIncrement = useMemo(() => increment, []); return <button onClick={memoizedIncrement}>{count}</button>; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: The button's click handler is memoized, improving performance

suggestedAnswer.text: None of the above
The button's click handler is re-created on every render
The counter doesn't increment due to an error in memoization

itemListElement.description: The useMemo hook memoizes the increment function, ensuring it is not re-created on every render, which can improve performance in certain scenarios.

itemListElement.text: What does the following React code do? ```const usePrevious = (value) => { const ref = useRef(); useEffect(() => { ref.current = value; }, [value]); return ref.current; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Returns the previous value of the passed state or prop

suggestedAnswer.text: None of the above
Stores the current value of the state or prop
Always returns 'undefined'

itemListElement.description: The custom hook usePrevious stores the previous value of the state or prop by updating a ref inside useEffect, and returning the ref's current value.

itemListElement.text:
What does the following React code do? ```const MyComponent = () => { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); useEffect(() => { const interval = setInterval(() => setCount(c => c + 1), 1000); return () => clearInterval(interval); }, []); return
{count}
; };```

acceptedAnswer.text: Starts an interval to increment the count every second and cleans up on unmount

suggestedAnswer.text: None of the above
Increments the count every second indefinitely
Logs the count to the console every second

itemListElement.description: The useEffect hook sets up an interval to increment the count every second, and cleans up the interval when the component unmounts.
